title: The authorization server returns a templated issuer instead of an identifier
rationale: R9.6, held down on a synthetic host so that the rule survives independently of any provider's document. `control-microsoft-entra-common-template-issuer` records the live instance this class was discovered from, but a captured document drifts -- providers edit their metadata -- and a rule whose only test is a capture is a rule that can be silently retired by someone else's deployment change. Two fixtures, one purpose: the control proves the class occurs in the wild, this one proves the instrument classifies it. Both matter, because the verdict before R9.6 existed was `same_host_different_path` -> FAIL_MISIMPLEMENTED, i.e. a MUST-level violation written against a deployment that is documented, deliberate and conforming on every tenant-specific path it serves.

spec.quote: The "issuer" value returned MUST be identical to the authorization server's issuer identifier value into which the well-known URI string was inserted to create the URL used to retrieve the metadata.  If these values are not identical, the data contained in the response MUST NOT be used.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 30 July 2026. This is the sentence R9.6 declines to apply here, and the reason is in its own wording: it compares against "the authorization server's issuer identifier value", and a value carrying a placeholder is not one.

spec.quote:
issuer
      REQUIRED.  The authorization server's issuer identifier, which is a URL that uses the "https" scheme and has no query or fragment components.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 30 July 2026. RFC 3986 §2 admits neither `{` nor `}` in a URI, so a templated value does not satisfy this definition -- the document is not conforming authorization-server metadata, but neither is it a mismatched identifier, and R6 assigns that gap to us rather than to the operator.

spec.quote: A URI is composed from a limited set of characters consisting of digits, letters, and a few graphic symbols.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 30 July 2026; `{` and `}` are outside that set and appear in no production of the URI grammar
